clue.text: Work out tennis score, keeping record ultimately

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: deuce is the tennis score of forty-all

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word record

explanation.surface: A tennis umpire works out the score while keeping a written record of play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts D, the last letter of 'record' (signalled by 'ultimately'), inside DEUCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce is to reason something out from evidence, a close synonym of working out.

clue.text: Cut up? Start to establish resolve

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: diced means cut into small cubes

indicators.note: start to signals the opening letter of the word establish

explanation.surface: A cryptic question about cutting followed by advice on firm resolve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' in a down clue turns DICED into DECID; 'Start to' gives E from 'establish'.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve as a verb means to make up one's mind, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Upsetting gibe about small gig at home

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a dig is a taunting remark, a gibe
S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a gig is a live music performance, a concert
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A performer is upset by a sneering comment about a modest house concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SCONCERTIN inside DIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disconcerting unsettles or perturbs, a direct synonym of upsetting.

clue.text: Red colour around borders regularly found

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for around
rims are edges or borders

indicators.note: regularly signals every other letter of the word found

explanation.surface: A red colour is often seen around the edges of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes alternate letters of 'found', giving ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Crimson is a deep shade of red, so it is a red colour.

clue.text: Take power, following church in law

indicators.note: in places the middle pieces within the word for law

parts.note: an act is a law passed by parliament

indicators.note: following puts the power letter after the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Someone seizes power under church law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' and 'in' are both placement signals: the first orders the two short pieces, the second sets that pair inside the word for law.
explanation.definitionFit: To take an offer or gift is to accept it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Primate in middle of sacred dance

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the letters taken from the other word
middle of takes the central two letters of the six-letter word sacred

parts.note: an ape is a primate

explanation.surface: A monkey joins in the middle of a holy ritual dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of' takes the central pair from a six-letter word; 'in' sets the primate inside that pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful skipping leap or frolic, a kind of dance step.

clue.text: Unusually quiet man rises in sport

indicators.note: unusually says the letters appear in an unusual order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusually quiet man stands up while playing a sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges QUIETMANRISES.
explanation.definitionFit: Equestrianism, riding and competing on horseback, is a sport.

clue.text: End appeal, wanting a drink

parts.note: a tip is the end of something, like a pencil tip

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a plea is an appeal

explanation.surface: Someone ends their plea because they want a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting a' drops A from PLEA, leaving PLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipple is an alcoholic drink, a person's habitual tipple.

clue.text: Dismiss teller

definitions.meaning: to ... an officer is to dismiss them from the armed forces
a teller is a bank employee handling cash

explanation.definitionFit: One word serves as a verb for sacking an officer and a noun for a bank clerk.

clue.text: Mean payment restricting wild spree

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for accommodation

indicators.note: wild signals the letters of the word spree run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: A miserly rent payment curbs someone's wild spending spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' reads as stingy, but here it is a verb, to signify. 'wild' gives EPRES and 'restricting' wraps the payment round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent something is to stand for or mean it, as a symbol does.

clue.text: Fruit, soft and round

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
P is piano, the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: A description of fruit that is soft and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like part of the fruit's description but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump means rounded and full in shape, a synonym of round.

clue.text: Rubbish in class ordinarily rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Ordinary rubbish is rejected in class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' marks SSORD hidden in 'class ordinarily'; 'rejected' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is waste matter or worthless stuff, a synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Study country while around lake

parts.note: Peru is a South American country

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word for while is read backwards

parts.note: as means while, as in 'as I was walking'
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone studies a country while travelling around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a containment signal, but nothing goes inside anything: it turns the word for while backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A perusal is a careful reading or examination, so a study of something.

clue.text: Chapter about gentle competitor

parts.note: on means about, as in a book on birds
tender means gentle or kind

explanation.surface: A book chapter about a gentle competitor.
explanation.definitionFit: A contender is a rival in a contest, a synonym of competitor.

clue.text: Lose hope, especially during bad raid

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so one piece sits inside the other
bad signals the letters of the word raid are spoiled into a new order

explanation.surface: People lose hope, particularly during a disastrous raid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' gives DAIR and 'during' places the abbreviation for especially within it.
explanation.definitionFit: To despair is to give up all hope, a direct equivalent phrase.

clue.text: Calmness in a place mob disrupted

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

indicators.note: disrupted signals the letters of the word mob are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone keeps calm where an unruly crowd causes disruption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges MOB into OMB.
explanation.definitionFit: Aplomb is self-assured composure, especially under pressure, so calmness.

clue.text: Land illuminated

definitions.meaning: to land or settle, as a bird does on a branch or a passenger from a bus

explanation.definitionFit: One word is a verb for touching down and an adjective for burning or lit.

clue.text: Short story, skilful on average

indicators.note: on in an across clue means placed after the other piece

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
able means skilful or competent

explanation.surface: A short-story writer is judged merely average in skill.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a brief tale told to teach a moral lesson, a kind of short story.

clue.text: Unspecified number in great old game

indicators.note: in puts the number letter inside the word for great

parts.note: big means great or large
N stands for an unspecified number in mathematics

explanation.surface: A traditional game played many times over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside BIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a game of chance where numbers are called and marked off cards.

clue.text: Act evasively, beginning to sound implausible

indicators.note: beginning to signals the first letter of the word sound

parts.note: tall as in a tall story means implausible or far-fetched

explanation.surface: Someone dodges questions, starting to sound unconvincing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' gives S from 'sound'.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to play for time and avoid committing, behaving evasively.

clue.text: Bulb working repeatedly, round one

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the pair of words wraps the single letter
repeatedly says the word for working appears twice

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A light bulb working again and again for one round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' gives ONON; 'round' places I in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion is a vegetable bulb, the swollen underground base of the plant.

clue.text: Time with group occupied by commercial business

indicators.note: occupied by means another piece sits inside the word for group

parts.note: a ring is a group or gang, such as a spy ring
an ad is a television commercial

explanation.surface: A firm's time spent with a group engaged in commerce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial' looks like an adjective but is the noun, a TV advert; 'occupied by' sets it inside the word for group.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading is buying and selling, the activity of commerce or business.

clue.text: Work on piece involving good part of circus

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the work piece after the rest
involving means taking in, so the letter goes inside the word for piece

parts.note: a bit is a piece
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Building work on a piece of circus equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' sets the letter for good inside the word for piece, and 'on' (an across clue) places the work after that.
explanation.definitionFit: The big top is the main tent of a circus, where performances happen.

clue.text: Part at end of concert on time

indicators.note: at end of places the part letters after the concert word

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, as in the BBC Proms

explanation.surface: A musician's part arrives at the end of a concert, on time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a famous London summer series of classical concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt as an adjective means punctual, arriving at the agreed hour.
